title: Shame and the Gospel
definition: Shame and the Gospel describes how the good news of Christ covers exposed, disgraced, and hiding sinners with mercy, righteousness, and belonging.
summary: Shame and the Gospel describes how the good news of Christ covers exposed, disgraced, and hiding sinners with mercy, righteousness, and belonging.
christFocus: Jesus bore shame, covers His people with righteousness, and welcomes the disgraced into His family.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Shame and the Gospel teaches that the Gospel answers not only guilt before God but also the hiding, exposure, and disgrace sin brings. Scripture tells the truth about humanity without denying dignity and without minimizing the ruin sin has brought.

God gives this truth so people may stop hiding and come into the light. People wounded by sin, rejection, abuse, disability, addiction, or failure may feel too dirty or unwanted to come near god. The Bible’s honesty is mercy because what remains hidden cannot be healed rightly.

Christ enters the truth this doctrine exposes. Jesus bore shame, covers His people with righteousness, and welcomes the disgraced into His family. In Him, sinners are not left under guilt, shame, bondage, fear, or death; they are called to repentance, faith, restoration, and new life by the power of the Holy Spirit.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People need this truth because sin, shame, weakness, and brokenness are not solved by denial. People wounded by sin, rejection, abuse, disability, addiction, or failure may feel too dirty or unwanted to come near god. Scripture tells the truth so that people may stop hiding and come to Christ.

It also protects believers from shallow answers. Humanity needs forgiveness, new birth, restoration, and Spirit-empowered obedience, not merely better circumstances or stronger willpower.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Step out of hiding toward Christ, truth, prayer, and safe fellowship. Bring this doctrine into prayer, Scripture, and daily obedience. Ask the Holy Spirit to make the truth real in your thinking, desires, relationships, and next faithful step with Christ.
